verdict.rationale: Groq's own models docs list OpenAI's open-weight GPT-OSS 120B, and community users report running Mixtral 8x7B, Llama 2 70B and Kimi K2 on its OpenAI-compatible API. This shows a multi-family open-weight catalog on shared on-demand endpoints, but the evidence does not show how broad or current the catalog is. Missing for 10: any evidence of Qwen or DeepSeek models, a first-party catalog listing showing breadth across current Llama and peer families, and explicit documentation that these models are served on shared serverless endpoints.

support.subject: As a developer, I can choose among a broad catalog of current open-weight model families (Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, GPT-OSS and peers) on shared serverless endpoints

citations.quote: GPT-OSS 120B is OpenAI's flagship open-weight language model with 120 billion parameters
I'm achieving consistent 450+ tokens/sec for Mixtral 8x7b 32k and ~200 tps for Llama 2 70B-4k.
I wanted to use Kimi K2 fast for coding and Groq was the only fast provider at the time
Flex processing is available for all models to paid customers only with 10x higher rate limits compared to on-demand processing.
